containerEngine.description:
This collector is designed to collect metadata from various container engines and provide a unified interface through the container plugin.
When enabled, it will deploy the container plugin and use it to collect metadata from the container engines.
Keep in mind that the old collectors (docker, containerd, crio, podman) will use the container plugin to collect metadata under the hood.

engines.description:
engines specify the container engines that will be used to collect metadata.
See https://github.com/falcosecurity/plugins/blob/main/plugins/container/README.md#configuration

hooks.description:
hooks specify the hooks that will be used to collect metadata from the container engine.
The available hooks are: create, start.
Some fields might not be available in create hook, but we are guaranteed that it gets triggered before first process gets started.

labelMaxLen.description:
labelMaxLen is the maximum length of the labels that can be used in the container plugin.
container labels larger than this value won't be collected.

pluginRef.description:
pluginRef is the OCI reference for the container plugin. It could be a full reference such as
"ghcr.io/falcosecurity/plugins/plugin/container:0.7.1". Or just name + tag: container:0.7.1.

withSize.description: withSize specifies whether to enable container size inspection, which is inherently slow.

kubernetes.description:
kubernetes holds the configuration for the kubernetes collector. Starting from version 0.37.0 of Falco, the legacy
kubernetes client has been removed. A new standalone component named k8s-metacollector and a Falco plugin have been developed
to solve the issues that were present in the old implementation. More info here: https://github.com/falcosecurity/falco/issues/2973

collectorHostname.description:
collectorHostname is the address of the k8s-metacollector. When not specified it will be set to match
k8s-metacollector service. e.x: falco-k8smetacollecto.falco.svc. If for any reason you need to override
it, make sure to set here the address of the k8s-metacollector.
It is used by the k8smeta plugin to connect to the k8s-metacollector.

collectorPort.description:
collectorPort designates the port on which the k8s-metacollector gRPC service listens. If not specified
the value of the port named `broker-grpc` in k8s-metacollector.service.ports is used. The default values is 45000.
It is used by the k8smeta plugin to connect to the k8s-metacollector.

enabled.description:
enabled specifies whether the Kubernetes metadata should be collected using the k8smeta plugin and the k8s-metacollector component.
It will deploy the k8s-metacollector external component that fetches Kubernetes metadata and pushes them to Falco instances.
For more info see:
https://github.com/falcosecurity/k8s-metacollector
https://github.com/falcosecurity/charts/tree/master/charts/k8s-metacollector
When this option is disabled, Falco falls back to the container annotations to grab the metadata.
In such a case, only the ID, name, namespace, labels of the pod will be available.

hostProc.description:
The plugin needs to scan the '/proc' of the host on which is running.
In Falco usually we put the host '/proc' folder under '/host/proc' so
the default for this config is '/host'.
The path used here must not have a final '/'.
Deprecated since falco 0.41.0 and k8smeta 0.3.0.

pluginRef.description:
--pluginRef is the OCI reference for the k8smeta plugin. It could be a full reference such as:
"ghcr.io/falcosecurity/plugins/plugin/k8smeta:0.4.1". Or just name + tag: k8smeta:0.4.1.

verbosity.description: verbosity level for the plugin logger: trace, debug, info, warning, error, critical.

containerSecurityContext.description: Set securityContext for the Falco container.For more info see the "falco.securityContext" helper in "pod-template.tpl"

customRules.description:
Third party rules enabled for Falco. More info on the dedicated section in README.md file.
Although Falco comes with a nice default rule set for detecting weird
behavior in containers, our users are going to customize the run-time
security rule sets or policies for the specific container images and
applications they run. This feature can be handled in this section.
Example:
rules-traefik.yaml: |-
[ rule body ]

falco.description:
Directly set values in the falco.yaml configuration file.
Please, note that some values may be overridden by other chart settings,
for specific features are managed by the chart itself. This includes:
- drivers configuration
- collectors configuration (this affects container and k8smeta plugins configurations)
- metrics configuration
Falco config files settings #

timeWindowSeconds.description: duration in seconds for the deduplication time window

printAllEvents.description: print in stdout all received events, not only those which match a rule

serviceMonitor.description: serviceMonitor holds the configuration for the ServiceMonitor CRD.

additionalLabels.description: additionalLabels specifies labels to be added on the Service Monitor.

enabled.description: enable the deployment of a Service Monitor for the Prometheus Operator.

interval.description: interval specifies the time interval at which Prometheus should scrape metrics from the service.

path.description: path at which the metrics are exposed

port.description: portname at which the metrics are exposed

relabelings.description: relabelings configures the relabeling rules to apply the target’s metadata labels.

scheme.description: scheme specifies network protocol used by the metrics endpoint. In this case HTTP.

scrapeTimeout.description:
scrapeTimeout determines the maximum time Prometheus should wait for a target to respond to a scrape request.
If the target does not respond within the specified timeout, Prometheus considers the scrape as failed for
that target.

targetLabels.description: targetLabels defines the labels which are transferred from the associated Kubernetes service object onto the ingested metrics.

tlsConfig.description:
tlsConfig specifies TLS (Transport Layer Security) configuration for secure communication when
scraping metrics from a service. It allows you to define the details of the TLS connection, such as
CA certificate, client certificate, and client key. Currently, the k8s-metacollector does not support
TLS configuration for the metrics endpoint.
insecureSkipVerify: false
caFile: /path/to/ca.crt
certFile: /path/to/client.crt
keyFile: /path/to/client.key

containerSecurityContext.description: containerSecurityContext holds the security settings for the container.

capabilities.description: capabilities fine-grained privileges that can be assigned to processes.

drop.description: drop drops the given set of privileges.

folder.description: folder where the dashboard is stored by grafana.

name.description: name specifies the name for the configmap.

namespace.description: namespace specifies the namespace for the configmap.

enabled.description: enabled specifies whether the dashboards should be deployed.

healthChecks.description: healthChecks contains the configuration for liveness and readiness probes.

livenessProbe.description: livenessProbe is a diagnostic mechanism used to determine wether a container within a Pod is still running and healthy.

httpGet.description: httpGet specifies that the liveness probe will make an HTTP GET request to check the health of the container.

port.description: port is the port on which the container exposes the "/healthz" endpoint.

periodSeconds.description: periodSeconds specifies the interval at which the liveness probe will be repeated.

readinessProbe.description: readinessProbe is a mechanism used to determine whether a container within a Pod is ready to serve traffic.

httpGet.description: httpGet specifies that the readiness probe will make an HTTP GET request to check whether the container is ready.

port.description: port is the port on which the container exposes the "/readyz" endpoint.

periodSeconds.description: periodSeconds specifies the interval at which the readiness probe will be repeated.

image.description: image is the configuration for the k8s-metacollector image.

pullPolicy.description: pullPolicy is the policy used to determine when a node should attempt to pull the container image.

pullSecrets.description: pullSecects a list of secrets containing credentials used when pulling from private/secure registries.

registry.description: registry is the image registry to pull from.

repository.description: repository is the image repository to pull from

tag.description: tag is image tag to pull. Overrides the image tag whose default is the chart appVersion.

nameOverride.description: nameOverride is the new name used to override the release name used for k8s-metacollector components.

namespaceOverride.description: namespaceOverride overrides the deployment namespace. It's useful for multi-namespace deployments in combined charts.

nodeSelector.description:
nodeSelector specifies a set of key-value pairs that must match labels assigned to nodes
for the Pod to be eligible for scheduling on that node.

podAnnotations.description: podAnnotations are custom annotations to be added to the pod.

podLabels.description: podLabels are labels to be added to the pod.

podSecurityContext.description: These settings are override by the ones specified for the container when there is overlap.

fsGroup.description: fsGroup specifies the group ID (GID) that should be used for the volume mounted within a Pod.

runAsGroup.description: runAsGroup specifies the group ID (GID) that the containers inside the pod should run as.

runAsNonRoot.description: runAsNonRoot when set to true enforces that the specified container runs as a non-root user.

runAsUser.description: runAsUser specifies the user ID (UID) that the containers inside the pod should run as.

replicaCount.description: replicaCount is the number of identical copies of the k8s-metacollector.

resources.description:
resources defines the computing resources (CPU and memory) that are allocated to the containers running within the Pod.
We usually recommend not to specify default resources and to leave this as a conscious
choice for the user. This also increases chances charts run on environments with little
resources, such as Minikube. If you do want to specify resources, uncomment the following
lines, adjust them as necessary, and remove the curly braces after 'resources:'.
limits:
cpu: 100m
memory: 128Mi
requests:
cpu: 100m
memory: 128Mi
